description: How the best math/CS textbooks (Halmos, Axler, SICP, Knuth, Feynman, Sipser, CLRS, MacKay, Pólya, Lakatos, Hersh) open a chapter, place worked examples and exercises, and state honest boundaries — applied to the Harbor Book's chapters. Use when drafting or reviewing a chapter opener, deciding where an exercise or worked example belongs, auditing a chapter's page grammar or claim-labeling, or running scripts/chapter_lint.py against a .tex chapter. NOT for the seven-moves result-writeup style (use harbor-exposition), figure drawing (use harbor-chartwork), or LaTeX build mechanics (use latex-whitepaper-engineering).
